title: Capacity reservation, weighted credit allocations, and plan sculpting PRD
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a new pricing and entitlement construct that allows customers to purchase capacity reservations (reserved throughput/requests) expressed as weighted credits, and to sculpt standard plans by mixing reserved buckets with on-demand usage. The goal is to provide predictable latency/capacity for high-value customers, reduce noisy-neighbor incidents, and enable more flexible billing that maps reserved capacity to invoice lines and prorations.

Problem statement:
- Large customers want guaranteed capacity (concurrency/throughput) for inference without overprovisioning GPU pools.
- Current plan model is flat: unit-based quotas + soft burst credits. We lack an ergonomic way to: 1) reserve a slice of shared Dedicated capacity tied to a plan; 2) allocate weighted credit currencies that cover mixed workloads (embeddings vs. generation tokens); 3) present clear invoice line items and prorations when reservation windows change mid-cycle.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Customers can purchase reservations expressed as weighted credits (e.g., 1 reservation credit = 1k embedding units OR 250 generation tokens depending on config).
- Reservation attaches to a plan and persists across billing cycles but supports mid-cycle adjustments and pro-rata billing.
- Reservations can be carved as 'isolated pool' or 'soft-reserve' (flexible reservation that drops to on-demand when contention is high).
- Billing system creates discrete invoice lines: reservation fee (recurring), usage consumed vs reservation, and overage lines with clear unit prices.
- Platform routing honors reservations with SLO prioritization; metrics available in Console and billing exports.

Scope (in-scope):
- API/Console UI for creating and managing reservations on subscription pages (create, modify qty, change mode: isolated vs soft-reserve).
- Backend entitlement layer: reservation tokens, weighted credit conversion table per model family, allocation engine to map requests to reserved vs on-demand buckets.
- Billing connector changes: invoice line item types for reservation, proration logic for mid-cycle quantity changes, reconciliation reports.
- Routing/runtime changes: priority queueing for reserved requests, observable tags in traces, cache/batch allocation accounting.

Out of scope for initial implementation:
- Marketplaces or reseller-managed reservations (follow-up phase).
- Complex per-route sculpting (first pass will allow plan-level reservations; route-level rules are future work).

Detailed requirements:
1) Reservation product model:
   - Reservation SKU = {name, unit_type, weight, price_monthly_per_unit, mode}. Unit types supported initially: GENERATION_TOKEN, EMBEDDING_UNIT, CONCURRENCY_SLOT.
   - Weighting table: mapping of model_category -> multiplier. Example: embeddings-v2 multiplier 1.0 for EMBEDDING_UNIT; codegen models may have generation_token multiplier 1.25. Table editable by PM with audit.

2) Entitlement & runtime mapping:
   - When a request arrives, allocator consults customer reservation balance (weighted credits) and attempt to debit the matching credit.
   - If in isolated mode and no credits left, request is queued/fails per customer's failure policy (configurable: queue-timeout, fallback-to-on-demand=false).
   - If in soft-reserve mode and no credits left, request is routed to on-demand pool with lower priority but still served. Metrics record "fellback_to_on_demand".

3) Billing & invoicing:
   - Monthly recurring charge for reserved units (qty * price_monthly_per_unit).
   - Usage reconciliation on invoice: show reservation consumption as "applied usage" (consumed units) and any overage charged at on-demand rate with clear line descriptions.
   - Mid-cycle changes: increasing reservation should prorate new units for remaining days. Decreasing reservation should credit pro-rata for unused days and generate a credit memo.

4) Console UX:
   - Subscription page shows reservation summary: units purchased, units consumed this cycle, forecasted consumption, and a one-click modify flow.
   - Observability: per-reservation metrics (consumption rate, drop-to-on-demand events), alerts when consumption > 80% of reserved capacity for 3 consecutive 5m windows.

5) API endpoints:
   - POST /subscriptions/{id}/reservations create reservation
   - PATCH /reservations/{id} update qty/mode
   - GET /subscriptions/{id}/reservations list
   - Usage export: reservations.csv with columns: date, reserved_units, consumed_units, overage_units, invoice_line_item_id

Acceptance criteria (testable):
- AC1: Create reservation via Console and API: a new reservation SKU appears on the subscription, recurring invoice line is generated for the next invoice cycle.
- AC2: Requests from a reserved customer are prioritized and debit weighted credits; consumption reduces reservation balance. Verified via logs and reservation consumption metric.
- AC3: Soft-reserve fallback: when reservation exhausted, subsequent requests are served by on-demand but flagged in traces and a Console metric increments.
- AC4: Isolated mode enforcement: when reservation exhausted and fallback disabled, requests are rejected with 429 and a clear error code.
- AC5: Mid-cycle increase: increasing reservation prorates the new reservation fee correctly on the next invoice and shows a prorated line item in preview.
- AC6: Mid-cycle decrease: decreasing reservation generates a credit memo equal to unused days * unit_price with explanation on invoice.
- AC7: Billing export aligns with usage export: each consumed unit in usage export maps to either reservation or overage line item; sum reconciles to invoice totals.
- AC8: Console alert fires when reservation consumption >80% sustained per configured window and an email is delivered to Account Owner.

Operational considerations & SLOs:
- Routing must guarantee that reserved requests meet the low-latency SLO for the plan tier (e.g., p95 < 120ms) unless isolation policy denies requests.
- Reconciliation job runs nightly to flag mismatched invoices and generate support tickets if >0.1% mismatch volume.

Rollout strategy:
- Beta: limited to sales-managed customers and internal Redwood tenants. Kick off with 3 customers representing different workloads (embeddings-heavy, token-heavy, concurrency-critical).
- Monitor: consumption patterns, fallback rates, and billing reconciliation accuracy for two billing cycles before general availability.

Telemetry & metrics to instrument:
- reservation.created, reservation.modified, reservation.deleted (with metadata).
- reservation.consumed_units (per-customer, per-SKU).
- reservation.fallback.count, reservation.isolated.reject.count.
- billing.proration.events, billing.credit_memos.created.

Security & compliance notes:
- Reservation metadata contains subscription identifiers and SKU mapping; ensure KMS encryption at rest in billing exports and mask PII in logs. Security review required prior to GA.

acceptance_criteria: Create/edit reservation from Console and API -> recurring invoice line created
Routing prioritizes reserved traffic and debits weighted credits as requests arrive
Soft-reserve mode falls back to on-demand and increments fallback metric
Isolated mode rejects excess traffic with 429 when fallback disabled
Proration on mid-cycle increase and credit memo on mid-cycle decrease visible in invoice preview
Usage export rows map to reservation or overage invoice lines and reconcile to invoice totals
Alerting triggers when consumption sustained >80% of reservation
Nightly reconciliation job covers invoicing mismatches and surfaces tickets for anomalies
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): enable feature flag for a small cohort (3 customers) for 2 billing cycles; monitor billing accuracy and routing behavior. Phase 2: open to all sales-approved customers and automate support playbooks for proration disputes. Phase 3: GA with console self-serve flows and documented runbooks.
open_questions: Should reservations support per-route allocation in v1 or be plan-level only? (proposal: plan-level only)
What is the authoritative weight table governance process (PM-owned with audit logs)?
What discounting model applies when customers commit to multi-month reserved quantities?
How do we surface reservation exhaustion in the SDKs/HTTP responses beyond 429? (error codes, Retry-After headers)
notes:
Decision log: 2025-11-20 engineering and finance agreed to use weighted credit model instead of separate SKUs per model family to reduce SKU sprawl. Finance requested explicit invoice line types for reservation recurring charges and prorations. Design to iterate small UX for initial Console flows.

Follow-ups: implement route-level sculpting (Q2), reseller marketplace support (Q3), automated savings recommendations in Optimize (Q4).
